# LIVER ABSCESS

[Oral step-down treatment](step-down-treatment)

Liver abscess should be suspected in all patients with fever, leukocytosis, and a space-occupying liver lesion. Liver abscesses fall broadly into two categories: pyogenic and amebic. In the United States, pyogenic liver abscess is much more common. Amebic liver abscess occurs almost exclusively in travelers and immigrants.

Infectious Diseases consultation is recommended due to prolonged treatment and need for follow-up.

## Duration of Therapy

A typical course for pyogenic liver abscess is 4 to 6 weeks based on improvement and follow-up imaging.

References:
Mandell chapter: Infections of the Liver and Biliary System
Sanford Guide article: Hepatic Abscess
Solomkin et al, Clin Infect Dis, 2010, 50:133-64
Up-to-Date article: Pyogenic liver abscess
Therapy:
Preferred:
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]

Critical illness or immunosuppression:
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h [R]

Alternative for critical illness or suppression:
Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]

Alternative for severe beta lactam reaction:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]
